problem: Traditional Siamese networks only decide 'same or different' for a pair of inputs, so they cannot distinguish multiple similar scene classes, which limits their use in indoor visual navigation.
motivation: Indoor visual navigation needs the agent to decide how to move from the current observation toward a target scene, which requires multi-class scene recognition from little data. Siamese networks handle small data and many categories well, so extending them beyond binary output is attractive.
key_idea: A Multi-State Siamese (MSS) network with a new loss that minimizes intra-category distance so that a Siamese architecture can classify multiple similar scene classes, and those scene classes guide navigation actions.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or detailed analysis can be cited. The abstract claims the loss makes the model converge and gives good recognition accuracy, and that classifying scenes is enough to guide the agent's movement.
method: Multi-State Siamese architecture: extends the two-class (same/different) Siamese network to distinguish multiple scene classes.
New loss function: minimizes the distance between samples of the same category during training.
Navigation via scene classification: classifies the current observation relative to the target scene to decide how the agent moves.
